items.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
items.raw_content: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.

items.title: Can AI help scientists identify promising drug candidates?
items.raw_content: MedChemBench evaluates how well AI models interpret molecular structures, reason from experimental evidence, and select compounds in early drug discovery.

items.title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents
items.title_zh: Epistemic Guard：面向工具型 Agent 的 MCP 凭证代理与来源门控记忆
items.raw_content: Epistemic Guard is an open-source Python library and out-of-process MCP receipt proxy that checks post-turn prose against signed tool receipts, gates SQLite memory writes by provenance and collapses syndicated RAG mirrors; it reports 93.2% accuracy at 17.9 ms median CPU latency and rejects all tampered receipts in its conformance suites.

items.title: Hebbia sees improvements in financial research with GPT-6 Astra
items.raw_content: Hebbia tested GPT-6 Astra for financial research. Its prerelease evaluations found gains in source coverage, citation relevance, and presentation quality.

items.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.raw_content:
Authors: Arshia Rafieioskouie, Matthew Lucas, Tzu-Han Hsu, Borzoo Bonakdarpour

Specification-guided reinforcement learning (RL) translates formal specifications of desired behavior of agents into shaped rewards. This paper introduces SLICR, a significant paradigm shift that advances the state of the art to specification-guided RL in adversarial settings under partial observability. We employ Strategy Logic (SL), which allows explicit quantification over agents' strategies and uses the linear temporal logic (LTL) to specify the agents' objectives and constraints. This enables reasoning not only about how agents should act to satisfy a specification, but also about how they should respond to the strategies and behaviors of other agents. We evaluate SLICR on three popular benchmarks: Predator-Prey, Google Research Football, and our home-grown extension of SMAC-HARD, demonstrating its effectiveness, scalability, and ability to adapt to diverse adversarial strategies.

items.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
items.raw_content:
Authors: Dylan Forde

Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage. On NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches 97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$ under pure task loss ($α=0$) and 98.83% at $α=0.05$ (matched by $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU at $α=0.05$, vs. 80.60% at $α=0$), while softmax-gated hub OT drops to 3.52%. In bidirectional operator microbenchmarks, our kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262\mathrm{K}$ (2.2x faster with 4.0x smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax) and 1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention at $L=4{,}096$; multi-layer LM runs use the unfused path. Zero-shot WikiText-103 multi-needle retrieval hits 100.00% (128/128 queries at $L=65\mathrm{K}$) vs. 0.78% for short-trained RoPE FlashAttention, and compact 4-layer WikiText-4K runs show modest causal and masked LM gains.

items.title: Who Grades the Agent? Privilege Separation for Coding-Agent Benchmarks
items.raw_content:
Authors: Nathan Nour Houlamy, Mattia Favretto, Earlence Fernandes, Mauro Conti

Benchmarks for AI-based coding agents are a staple of the current AI landscape, because they are the leading way to measure the performance of LLMs. Their scores guide business and research decisions. Evaluating coding agents is challenging, since they are able to manipulate their evaluation infrastructure to artificially achieve better scores. Grading an agent's solution often requires running its code, which can then manipulate the evaluation process. BenchJack, an automated benchmark auditor, recently reached near-perfect scores on nine of ten popular agent benchmarks without actually solving their tasks. Agents already do this unprompted, as OpenAI's July 2026 Hugging Face incident showed.
  Building on secure systems design, we introduce SplitBench, a privilege separation framework for evaluating coding agents and the first in the scientific literature to separate running a task's tests from judging their results. Even an agent whose code takes over the entire test environment cannot forge a pass, because a trusted grader holds the expected answers. We show that real-world benchmarks (e.g., Terminal-Bench, DeepSWE) can be ported to the SplitBench framework with minimal effort and high fidelity: 180 of 202 tasks convert, and SplitBench agrees with the native graders on 98.7% of agent attempts. We attack the converted tasks in the worst case, where adversarial agents can read all the grading code but not the expected answers. SplitBench blocked 75% of their attempts; the rest mostly reveal weaknesses in the original tasks' tests rather than flaws in SplitBench.

items.title: A Nepali-Accented English Evaluation Dataset for Automatic Speech Recognition
items.raw_content:
Authors: Santosh Dahal, Kiran Chandra Dahal

Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems perform strongly on native-English benchmarks, yet their accuracy degrades sharply when the input speech comes from under represented non-native accents. Nepali-accented English is particularly under-served: existing resources either focus on native Nepali speech, cover broader multi-accent settings without dedicated Nepali evaluation, or provide only limited Nepali-accent coverage. This paper presents a Nepali-accented English evaluation dataset designed to support robust ASR benchmarking under accent mismatch. The corpus was collected through a web-based platform that did not collect directly identifying metadata and contains recordings from 57 speakers. Each session follows a fixed 22-prompt protocol consisting of 11 phonetic prompts, 10 domain prompts, and 1 spontaneous prompt, providing complementary coverage of pronunciation, topical vocabulary, and natural speaking style. In addition to transcribed speech, the dataset includes participant metadata for coarse exploratory subgroup analysis and speaker-level manual recording-quality labels. Manual quality assessment shows that 50.9% of sessions are clean and 42.1% contain only mild noise. As a descriptive reference, open-source ASR baselines are substantially worse on this corpus than the corresponding LibriSpeech test-clean values reported in official model cards, reaching 38.15-55.00% WER on the collected set versus reported 2-4% WER on LibriSpeech test-clean. These baseline results position the corpus as a practical held-out resource for evaluating accent robustness and out-of-distribution generalization on Nepali-accented English.

items.title: DM-Lab at TREC 2026 RAG: Multi-Query Retrieval, Ensemble Judging, and Claim-Pack Generation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Elyas Irankhah, Muhammad Arif, Sreeraj Ramachandran, Samah Fodeh-Jarad

We present DM-Lab-RAG-2026, a framework developed for the TREC 2026 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) track. The framework integrates large-scale evidence retrieval and citation-grounded answer generation over the 553-million-document ClimbMix-400B corpus. The retrieval architecture combines multi-query BM25, reciprocal rank fusion, ensemble relevance assessment, listwise reranking, and adaptive retrieval depth. The generation pipeline employs a claim-first strategy to extract evidence-linked atomic claims, construct cited responses, and verify source support. Across 22 development topics, the retrieval system achieved a mean nDCG@30 of 0.604. In the official evaluation, it attained a set precision of 0.455 and a manual nugget gain of 0.910. Additional experiments examine the influence of reranking, evidence selection, and citation verification on system performance. The evaluation demonstrates the potential of diversified lexical retrieval and language-model-based relevance assessment for large-scale evidence discovery. It further identifies evidence preservation and structured answer construction as key considerations for reliable RAG. This work provides a reproducible framework for investigating retrieval effectiveness and evidence-grounded generation.

items.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
items.raw_content:
Authors: Kelvin Kiu-Wai Tam, Newt Hue-Nam K. Nguyen, Tianshi Zheng, Yunxiang Mo, Weihan Li et al.

Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. However, existing agents rely on harnesses that combine multiple mechanisms, making it difficult to determine how individual components contribute to performance. We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it stores and reuses lessons from those attempts. Across MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol, we isolate the effects of individual harness design choices by evaluating each against a recency-truncation baseline within a shared agent framework. For context management, we find that preserving individually accessible records of past attempts is more effective than maintaining a rolling summary, with context folding performing best across all six settings and improving upon the baseline by up to 19.2%. For skill management, selectively discarding persistently unused lessons is more effective on average than consolidating them or promoting them to standing rules. Building on these findings, we combine context folding and skill deletion in MLEvolver, which achieves a 72.7% medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite and a 94% $\mathrm{fast}_1$ score on KernelBench Level 3, substantially outperforming AIDE and OpenEvolve under the same inference budget. Overall, our study distills design principles for preserving experimental history and curating reusable lessons in autoresearch harnesses, paving the way for agents that turn accumulated experience into sustained progress.

items.title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
items.raw_content:
Authors: Mohammad Alijanpour Shalmani, Alale Rezvani Boroujeni, Ali Amini

Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them. We present DiTraR, which addresses video selection from two complementary directions. A witness-interval scorer decomposes the query into probes and scores every candidate interval of every corpus video exactly; a multi-scorer energy ensemble averages the energies of independently trained scorers before one exhaustive search; and a transcript verifier, a frozen language model that reads the time-stamped dialogue of the highest-ranked videos, re-orders the moments without changing their boundaries. With all settings frozen on development data and a single evaluation, DiTraR reaches 24.36 and 13.55 R@1 at IoU 0.5 and 0.7 on the TVR validation split. The ensemble improves queries about visual content, the verifier improves queries about dialogue, and their gains largely add up.

items.title: Engram: Multi-Stage Memory for Agentic Tuning of Heterogeneous Models
items.raw_content:
Authors: Huanran Li, Nhat X. T. Le, Kevin De Angeli, Yao Xuan, Alireza Vahdatpour et al.

Large language model (LLM) agents can now tune neural networks, yet without cross-session memory they spend costly trials rediscovering known lessons. Reuse is difficult because production models differ in architecture, training setup and inference budget. We present Engram, a memory system that links past trial outcomes with the hypotheses and rationale behind them and assesses whether this evidence applies to the current model. An online agent curates evidence at the decision points where it is needed: Initial Guidance supplies validated lessons at the start, Session Retrieval supplies related past sessions before each batch of hypotheses is generated, and Trial Candidate Review checks each trial candidate against matching past trials. Between sessions, an offline agent distills validated lessons, making the memory self-improving. On two ads models, Engram reaches the 32-trial result of a no-memory control with 47% fewer trials and also ends with a better model on average.

items.title: Felid: A Flexible and Efficient Design for Transformer Fine-Tuning over Encrypted Data
items.title_zh: Felid：面向加密数据的 Transformer 微调高效方案
items.raw_content: Felid targets ciphertext-level bottlenecks in fully homomorphic encryption training, using flexible packing, operation-specific matrix evaluation and functional bootstrapping to cut ciphertext rotations and relinearizations by 30x and bootstrapping invocations by 2.5x, completing fine-tuning of a 2-layer BERT-style model with batch size 16 in 650 seconds for an 8x speedup.

items.title: Mind the Delta: Early Pruning of RTL Variants for Agentic Hardware Optimization
items.title_zh: Mind the Delta：面向 Agent 硬件优化的 RTL 变体早期剪枝
items.raw_content: DiffScope is a training-free anytime selection framework that races full synthesis runs in parallel and uses live area telemetry plus the base design's trajectory to stop uncompetitive RTL variants early; across 43 design families it recovered the exhaustive-synthesis optimum in every family while cutting total evaluation work by 44.9%.

items.title: Taking the PULSE of Enterprise Workflows: Evaluating Persistent Project-State Understanding
items.title_zh: PULSE：评估企业工作流中的持续项目状态理解
items.raw_content: PULSE is a benchmark of 1,573 questions over 30 enterprise project histories that evaluates open loops, project evolution and view gaps; the authors find substantial headroom for retrieval, graph- and memory-augmented retrieval, and long-context systems, and show that providing explicit project state on top of gold evidence yields further gains.

items.title: Correct Precedents Induce Policy Violations in On-Device LLM Agents
items.title_zh: 正确先例反而诱发违规：端侧 LLM Agent 的策略失效
items.raw_content: The paper identifies correct-precedent generalization, where an on-device agent that correctly releases an item whose restriction was lifted becomes more likely to release the next still-restricted item, finding the failure in 13 open-weight models from nine developers; Paired Decision Distillation restores the safe rate to nearly 100% in every distilled model without extra prompts or model calls.

items.title: Mjolnir: Finding and Reproducing Vulnerabilities in Root-of-Trust Firmware and RTL with Project-Grounded Agents
items.title_zh: Mjolnir：用项目语境 Agent 发现并复现信任根固件与 RTL 漏洞
items.raw_content: Mjolnir is an agentic pipeline that gives discovery and skeptical-review agents each project's threat model and design conventions, then reproduces surviving findings as proof-of-concept tests; evaluated on six firmware and RTL targets in Caliptra, OpenTitan and OpenPRoT, its findings include 64 previously unknown security-relevant bugs confirmed by maintainers.

items.title: Security Bite Podcast: Not amused, two months of Meta Muse privacy problems
items.title_zh: Security Bite 播客：Meta Muse 两个月隐私风波未平
items.raw_content: The episode recaps two months of security and privacy problems around Meta's Muse AI agent, which has passed 10 million downloads, from the 'not-a-mused' zero-day to its former security chief calling it 'totally insane' to trust AI agents with passwords and finances, and a Reuters report that Meta employees raised alarms.

items.title: Toward Adversarially Robust World Models
items.title_zh: 迈向对抗鲁棒的世界模型
items.raw_content: The paper introduces state hallucination and dynamic shift attacks against latent dynamic world models, argues that robust latent-space encoders are the key component of robust world models, and shows improved robustness from adversarial encoder training across four model families including DINO World Model, Le World Model, r2Dreamer and Cosmos 3.
